tasks.short: Direct the HR team's daily work on hiring, pay, absence and labour relations.

today.trigger: The working day starts, a site manager escalates, or the payroll, absence or vacancy calendar shows something due.
steps: Ask the HR business partners and specialists what is stuck in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
Sort the list across hiring, pay, absence files, the works council and complaints.
Assign an owner and a deadline in the team meeting or by Teams.
Step in when a manager conflict or a labour-relations point needs the director.
Chase items still open at the end of the week.
drudgery: Chasing status across five systems and three sites.
Rewriting the same weekly note for the management team.
Rebuilding the picture of who owns an absence file or an offer.
today.time_sinks: Most of the lost time goes to reconstructing the picture before a useful conversation can start.

lenses.faster: The morning picture is already on one page, so the 'where do we stand' round drops out of the stand-up. The director uses the meeting to assign owners and handle the items that need a judgement.
lenses.autonomous: After the nightly AFAS refresh, a brief lists only breaches: vacancies past the agreed age, week-one onboarding incomplete, Wet verbetering poortwachter deadlines inside two weeks, expired certificates, and payroll blockers.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the coordination cost, each site would run the same brief, and the director would see next week's load for hiring and absence across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
lenses.joy: Status chasing and the rewritten weekly note are the parts nobody will miss. The conversation with an HR business partner about a manager, a conflict or a works-council worry stays.
lenses.options: For a peak week the brief can lay out three workable responses, such as overtime within the CAO, a flex order, or moving people between Tilburg and Venlo, each with cost and roster effects.
lenses.altitude: The director sets the thresholds and, once a month, checks whether the brief changed what the team did. Assembly of the status picture sits with the system.
reach: The weekly commentary the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst now holds back for a meeting.
First sort of site escalations that are status, which today wait for an HR business partner to retell them.
A people-operations note for the Finance Director built from the same exception list.

tasks.human_edge: Twelve colleagues take direction from a person who knows the three sites and will back them with the works council and the management team. That trust, and the choice of which conflict to take personally, stays with the director.
tasks.pattern_why: This is daily direction of people. A prepared picture and a written assignment make the meeting shorter. Priorities, tone and labour-relations calls stay with the director, which matches a low chance that AI can do nearly all of it.

in_practice.trigger: Each weekday at 07:30 after the nightly AFAS extract has refreshed Power BI, and whenever an HR business partner or the works council marks a Teams item urgent.
steps: Pull breaches from Power BI, Recruitee and Studytube: vacancy age, unsigned offers, week-one onboarding, poortwachter deadlines, certificates, payroll-close items.
Draft a one-page stand-up note with site, owner and the ask.
The director reorders the list and assigns in the stand-up.
Owners and deadlines go to the Teams HR channel and a SharePoint action list.
Anything still open after five days returns to the director's calendar.
in_practice.human_gate: The director sets the day's priorities and approves anything sent to a warehouse manager, the works council, a union or a staffing agency.
data_needed: Vacancy age and stage in Recruitee
Offer acceptance and start dates
Week-one onboarding checklist
Absence-file deadlines without medical content
Forklift, VCA and food-safety expiry dates
Payroll close calendar and open blockers
Who on the HR team is in or out this week
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint HR action list and the Teams HR-leads channel, dated, with the owner.

evidence.claim: Power BI can push a scheduled view of a nightly AFAS extract and alert when a measure crosses a threshold the director has set.
Microsoft 365 Copilot can summarise an Outlook and Teams thread into a short note the director edits before anyone acts on it.
A works council often has a consent right when an employer introduces a system that monitors staff or processes employee personal data.

risks: The brief becomes a second report nobody trusts if AFAS contract type, cost centre or absence status is coded loosely.
A wide Teams channel with absence deadlines or individual performance can breach AVG and worry the works council; medical content from the bedrijfsarts does not belong in it.
If the brief is used to score the HR team, it slides into personnel monitoring and needs works-council consent under the WOR.
People stop raising a messy problem because it was not on the exception list.
research_questions: What share of the Monday meeting is spent reconstructing status, and what share is already a decision?
Which AFAS fields for contract type, site, cost centre and absence-file status are complete enough to trust a threshold?
Does the works council already have an agreement that covers HR dashboards containing absence deadlines?
Which escalations last month were status, and which needed the director in the room?

tasks.short: Advise managers on equal treatment, unwanted conduct and the policy change that follows.

today.trigger: A manager asks what the rule is, or a case of unequal treatment or unwanted conduct reaches HR.
steps: Find the current policy on SharePoint, the relevant CAO clause and the complaint procedure.
Talk with the manager, usually with the HR business partner for that site.
Decide whether this is advice, a formal complaint, a confidential-counsellor route or a works-council matter.
Recommend a policy change when the same question keeps returning.
Check that Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo are applying the same rule.
drudgery: Searching for the current version of a policy or house rule.
Writing the same explanation of equal treatment, roster fairness or flex versus permanent again.
Reconstructing how a similar case was handled at another site.
today.time_sinks: Finding the clause and writing the note takes as long as the conversation with the manager.

lenses.faster: The policy clause, the CAO article and the last anonymised similar case are already in the pack, so the search and the first draft drop out. The meeting with the manager stays.
lenses.autonomous: A repeated question, such as a third ask in a month about the same roster or flex rule, opens a change note and puts it on the director's list without waiting for someone to remember.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, every manager would get a written answer in the same week, and recurring questions would become one policy update the works council sees, applied the same way on all three sites.
lenses.joy: Hunting the current PDF and retyping the same explanation are the parts nobody will miss. The careful conversation about a person's treatment, and the call on what is fair, stay.
lenses.options: The pack can offer several responses side by side: apply the existing rule, clarify the house rule, change the policy, train the managers, or open the formal complaint route.
lenses.altitude: The director maintains the approved policy set, the sources the drafter may use, and a monthly review of where advice differed by site. Drafting the first pack sits with the system.
reach: First-line answers the HR business partners already give when the question is a settled rule.
A CAO check the Compensation and Benefits Specialist can sign before a pay or roster question reaches the director.
A single policy-gap list for the works council, in place of three site versions of the same problem.

tasks.human_edge: A manager accepts hard advice from a director who will say the same thing in the works council and, if needed, to a union or an insurer. The confidential counsellor's conversations and any hearing stay with people, because trust and liability sit there.
tasks.pattern_why: The advice pack is documents in, a structured recommendation out: clause, scope, options, and a proposed change. It becomes Noordhaven's advice only when the director sends it. Equal treatment and unwanted conduct are too exposed to run unattended.

in_practice.trigger: A manager's question is logged, or a complaint or counsel intake is opened by an HR business partner.
steps: Retrieve only the current SharePoint policy, the complaint procedure, the applicable CAO extract and anonymised prior positions.
Draft a one-page pack: the question, the clause, who is in scope (permanent, fixed-term, flex), options, and a recommended change if the rule is unclear.
Flag if the matter belongs with the confidential counsellor, the bedrijfsarts route, or the formal complaint procedure.
The director edits and either answers the manager or sends the HR business partner with an approved line.
A question that recurs three times opens a policy-change item for the works council where consent or advice is required.
in_practice.human_gate: Nothing goes to a manager, an employee or the works council until the director approves the text. A sanction, a dismissal or a finding about a named person is always a human decision.
data_needed: Current, owner-marked policies and the complaint procedure
The CAO articles that cover the topic, with version and date
Contract type and site of the people concerned, not the medical file
Anonymised record of earlier positions
Whether the works council has a consent right on that regulation
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint advice log with the question, the sources cited, the director's decision and the date. Case detail stays in the restricted HR folder.

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot can draft from policy documents the company already stores in SharePoint, and the director can open the source file beside the draft.
Dutch employers have a duty under the Working Conditions Act to manage psychosocial workload, including unwanted conduct, and to work with a policy and a route for employees.
An AI tool that proposes a measure affecting a named worker can fall in the EU AI Act employment category and needs a real human decision before it counts.

risks: A invented clause or CAO article number reads as confident and is wrong. The director must see the source text.
Questions about a named person, health or unwanted conduct are sensitive personal data under the AVG and do not belong in an open prompt or a wide channel.
A manager may treat the draft as permission to skip the complaint procedure or the confidential counsellor.
The same facts get a different answer in Venlo and Rotterdam if the approved line is not logged.
research_questions: What share of manager questions last quarter were repeats of a settled rule, and what share were new cases about a person?
Are the complaint procedure, house rules and both CAOs on SharePoint current, with a named owner and a version date?
Will managers wait for an approved answer, or will they copy a draft straight into a letter to an employee?
What does the external labour lawyer or the insurer require before a written position is sent on equal treatment or unwanted conduct?

tasks.short: Find what the people numbers show and recommend what to change.

today.trigger: The monthly management report, a spike in absence or early leavers, or preparation for the works council.
steps: Open the Power BI HR dashboards on the nightly AFAS extract, then export to Excel when the cut is missing.
Split figures by site, team, contract type and, where the data allow, flex versus permanent.
Test a suspected cause with the HR business partner for that site.
Write a recommendation on policy, hiring or a manager's practice.
Present the story to the management team or the works council.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same cuts in Excel because the dashboard answers a different question.
Adding flex workers by hand because they sit in agency portals, not in the AFAS headcount.
Writing the narrative again each month from a fresh export.
today.time_sinks: Cleaning and re-cutting the data, then explaining small noisy movements as if they were a cause.

lenses.faster: The standard cuts, 90-day retention, time to hire, offer acceptance, week-one onboarding and verzuim by site, are calculated before the director asks. The director starts at the interpretation.
lenses.autonomous: A move past an agreed threshold, such as 90-day retention on a shift or short-term absence on a team, opens a dated note after the nightly refresh and assigns it to the site HR business partner.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, every team lead would see a stable monthly page on retention, absence and certificate gaps for their own team, and the director would spend the cycle on the few patterns that repeat across sites.
lenses.joy: Exporting, pivoting and reformatting are the parts nobody will miss. The discussion with a site lead about why new pickers leave in the first ninety days stays.
lenses.options: Each notable move can come with several plausible readings, for example roster, pay step, agency mix or a single manager, each with the comparison that would support or weaken it.
lenses.altitude: The director agrees the definitions with People Analytics, including what 'productive at day 90' means, and reviews misses and small-cell suppressions. Building the monthly cut sits with the analyst and the model.
reach: The monthly note the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst already drafts, read by the director as a decision paper.
The verzuim-cost paragraph the Controller needs in the finance pack, using the same definitions.
A site page the HR business partner can use without asking for a fresh export.

tasks.human_edge: Deciding that a pattern is real, and that a manager or a policy should change because of it, depends on site knowledge and on someone who will defend the recommendation to the works council. The figures do not make that judgement.
tasks.pattern_why: The rates themselves are a calculation on structured data. A cause is only a hypothesis, labelled with the comparison that supports it, and a recommendation changes personnel practice only after the director agrees. That is a gated workflow, not a dashboard left to speak for itself.

in_practice.trigger: The morning after the nightly Power BI refresh, and immediately when 90-day retention, time to hire or verzuim crosses a threshold the director has set.
steps: Refresh the agreed cuts: site, role family, tenure, contract type, and flex versus permanent where the agency data has been loaded.
Suppress groups below the cell size the privacy officer has set, and keep diagnoses out of the file.
Draft a short note: what moved, since when, the two or three hypotheses, and the comparison that would decide between them.
The director and the site HR business partner accept, reject or amend the recommendation.
The accepted action, its owner and the review date go to the SharePoint action list.
in_practice.human_gate: A recommendation that changes a policy, a roster practice or a manager's targets is issued only after the director signs it. Figures below the agreed cell size are not shown.
data_needed: AFAS headcount, contract type, site, function and start date
Leavers in the first 90 days and stated exit reason
Time to hire, offer acceptance and week-one onboarding from Recruitee
Verzuim rates without medical data
Certificate expiries from Studytube
Agency hours by site, so flex workers are in the base
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint 'People analysis' folder, one dated note per decision, next to the Power BI report version it used.

evidence.claim: Power BI already supports the nightly AFAS HR dashboards this company uses, including filters, measures and scheduled refresh.
AFAS Profit holds the contract, organisation and absence records needed for cohort rates, with absence kept separate from medical data held by the bedrijfsarts.
Observational HR data can show where a rate moved and for whom. Naming a cause from that cut alone is a weak inference and needs a check with someone who knows the site.

risks: A shift that looks like a management problem is an older workforce, a harder client or a coding change in AFAS.
Small teams make a verzuim cut identifiable, which collides with AVG and with what the works council will accept.
Flex workers are 150 to 300 people and sit mainly in agency portals, so an AFAS-only story misses a large part of the warehouse.
The nightly refresh is a day behind, and payroll or absence entry after month close can rewrite the story.
research_questions: Which people problems did the director actually investigate in the last two quarters, and which report did they open?
Are exit reasons, agency hours and function codes present and usable, or only permanent-staff headcount?
What minimum group size does the privacy officer, and the works council, accept for a verzuim or retention cut?
How much of these 185 hours duplicates a note the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst already writes?

tasks.short: Plan and steer training, personnel and labour relations across the three sites.

today.trigger: The monthly planning cycle, a CAO change, a works-council agenda, or a certificate deadline before peak season.
steps: Set the quarter's priorities for hiring, training and labour relations with the specialists.
Check Studytube for missing or expired forklift, VCA and food-safety certificates.
Align the works-council calendar with roster, privacy and policy items that need advice or consent.
Hand CAO changes to payroll and compensation as concrete work.
Review at month end whether the plan happened.
drudgery: Maintaining a spreadsheet of who may not be scheduled because a certificate lapsed.
Repeating the same priorities in three site conversations.
Collecting progress by hand from L&D, payroll, compensation and the HR business partners.
today.time_sinks: The follow-up on completion takes longer than the decision about what the quarter is for.

lenses.faster: The certificate gaps, the open CAO actions and the works-council agenda arrive as one monthly pack. Collecting progress from four specialists drops out of the director's week.
lenses.autonomous: A certificate that will expire before the next peak, or a poortwachter deadline with no owner, opens a task for L&D or the site HR business partner as soon as Studytube or AFAS shows it.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, Noordhaven would run a live rule that nobody is planned onto a shift without a valid certificate, and every CAO change would have an owner before payroll runs.
lenses.joy: Chasing completion lists is the part nobody will miss. The works-council meeting and the conversation with a union official about the warehouse CAO stay.
lenses.options: The quarterly plan can show several mixes of permanent hiring, flex and training capacity, with the effect on week-one onboarding and on who is allowed to drive a forklift in November.
lenses.altitude: The director sets the operating calendar and the gates, such as no go-live of a vacancy without a function code, and reviews exceptions. Chasing the specialists for status sits with the calendar.
reach: The compliance calendar and the chase, which today sit with the two Learning and Development Specialists, while course design stays with them.
The CAO implementation checklist the Payroll Specialist and the Compensation and Benefits Specialist rebuild at each change.
The site certificate list an HR business partner needs before a roster is agreed.

tasks.human_edge: What the quarter is for, and how hard to push a works-council or union point, is a judgement about relationships and about the 90-day north star. A calendar cannot hold that conversation.
tasks.pattern_why: The director still plans and steers the function. The gain is a prepared calendar and an exception list for training, CAO follow-through and works-council items. Direction of the specialists and the labour-relations stance stay in the room.

in_practice.trigger: The first working day of the month, a published CAO or statutory change, and any Studytube certificate due to expire within 60 days.
steps: Build the monthly pack: certificate gaps by site and role, open CAO actions, poortwachter files with an administrative deadline and no owner, works-council items due.
Draft a proposed priority order tied to peak season and to the 90-day north star.
The director agrees the month's plan with L&D, payroll, compensation and the three HR business partners.
Owners and dates are written to the SharePoint HR calendar.
Items that would block a shift or a payroll run are reviewed weekly. Exceptions are explicit.
in_practice.human_gate: The director approves the month's priorities and any item that goes to the works council, a union or a change in who is allowed to work a shift.
data_needed: Studytube enrolments, completions and expiry dates for forklift, VCA and food safety
AFAS function and site, so the certificate can be tied to a person who is scheduled
Open CAO actions and their payroll effective dates
Works-council agenda and which items need consent or advice
Administrative owners of absence files, without medical content
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint HR operating calendar, one row per action with owner, site and due date.

evidence.claim: Studytube stores enrolments, completions and certificate status for the mandatory courses this company already runs.
AFAS Profit can list employees by function and site so a certificate gap can be tied to a role that needs it.
Training rules, working time and absence policy are typical works-council consent topics, so a new gate on scheduling has an OR route as well as a system route.

risks: There is no workforce-management system in the stack, so a certificate gate cannot by itself stop a shift being planned. Someone still has to act on the list.
A chase tool that ranks HR specialists on task completion is personnel monitoring and needs works-council consent.
CAO follow-through that starts before the text is final will put the wrong scale into AFAS.
Peak season will overwhelm a monthly cycle if the only review is monthly.
research_questions: Who today prevents an employee with an expired forklift, VCA or food-safety certificate from being planned, and in which system?
How many certificate gaps and poortwachter files had no named owner at the last peak?
Which of these hours are the plan, and which are the director repeating the plan in three site meetings?
Which labour-relations items last year truly needed the director, against items payroll could have closed from a checklist?

tasks.short: Prepare the personnel budget and follow it through the year.

today.trigger: The budget round, the monthly close, or a forecast revision from finance.
steps: Take payroll actuals and the HR cost centres from AFAS.
Add vacancies, agency spend, training, the arbodienst and the expected CAO increase in Excel.
Compare with the FP&A forecast and explain the gap.
Re-forecast the rest of the year, including the flex swing.
Report the personnel-operations budget to the Finance Director.
systems: Staffing agency invoices in accounts payable
drudgery: Copying actuals into a workbook only the director can follow.
Reconciling three agency invoices with the flex plan.
Explaining vakantiegeld, shift allowances and employer charges again each cycle.
today.time_sinks: Assembly and reconciliation, concentrated in the budget round and again at each month close.

lenses.faster: Actuals, known vacancies and booked agency cost land in a standard variance pack, so the director stops rebuilding the workbook. The time goes to the gap that needs a decision.
lenses.autonomous: After each AFAS month close, a variance note is waiting when a cost centre or the agency total moves past the threshold agreed with FP&A. Nobody has to remember to pull it.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the assembly cost, finance and HR would keep one monthly people-cost view, by site and by permanent versus flex, accurate enough to place the next agency order on purpose.
lenses.joy: Copying ledgers and chasing which invoice belongs to which site are the parts nobody will miss. The argument about whether to add a recruiter, a trainer or another flex block stays.
lenses.options: The pack can show several year-end paths, for example fill with permanent staff, cover the peak with flex at pay-parity cost, or defer a vacancy, each with employer charges and CAO allowances.
lenses.altitude: The director agrees the drivers and the threshold with FP&A and reviews the monthly exceptions. Maintaining the workbook sits with the model that finance already refreshes.
reach: The people-cost phasing the FP&A Analysts now build from a separate headcount file.
A monthly personnel-cost variance note the Controller can drop into the close pack.
A flex-versus-permanent view the Finance Director asks for at budget time, with agency invoices included.

tasks.human_edge: Choosing where to spend the HR budget, and what workforce bet to defend to the Finance Director, is a management call. The pack can price the options. It cannot choose the one the company will stand behind.
tasks.pattern_why: The arithmetic of actuals, vacancies and agency invoices is structured and checkable, and the director remains responsible for the budget. A draft pack makes the review faster. Publishing a forecast into the company's numbers stays a human decision shared with FP&A.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS month close completing, and the budget calendar date set by the Finance Director.
steps: Load payroll actuals, HR cost centres, open vacancies and booked agency invoices into the variance pack.
Separate the movements that are timing, such as vakantiegeld and shift allowances, from movements in heads or rates.
Draft a short explanation of each gap over the threshold, with a proposed full-year view.
The director reviews the pack with FP&A and amends the assumptions.
The agreed version is stored and used in the next management report.
in_practice.human_gate: The director and FP&A both sign the version that enters the company forecast. A hire, a flex block or a training spend above the agreed limit still needs the normal approval.
data_needed: Payroll actuals and employer charges by cost centre and site
Headcount and FTE by function and contract type
Recruitee vacancies and accepted offers not yet in payroll
Agency invoices and hours by site for all three agencies
CAO increase, vakantiegeld month and shift-allowance rules
The FP&A forecast version this must agree to
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint budget folder, one workbook version per month, with the assumption log on the first sheet.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit posts payroll and supplier invoices into the general ledger, so personnel actuals and agency cost already sit in finance.
Power BI on the nightly AFAS extract can present a monthly variance against a budget table without a fresh manual export.
A driver-based personnel budget, built from heads, scale, allowances, employer charges and agency hours, is ordinary FP&A practice and can be checked line by line.

risks: HR and FP&A keep two forecasts if ownership of the drivers is not agreed, and the management team will not know which one to trust.
Agency invoices arrive late, so the flex cost in the close is wrong in the month the peak actually happened.
A workbook at employee level exposes salaries. The pack needs a threshold below which a site or role is grouped, under AVG.
A CAO increase that is not yet in the AFAS scales will make the rest-of-year view look better than payroll can deliver.
research_questions: Who owns the personnel forecast today, the HR director or FP&A, and which workbook does the Finance Director actually use?
Are shift allowances, vakantiegeld, employer charges and the three agencies visible as separate AFAS accounts?
How large was the flex-invoice timing gap at the last three month closes?
What variance would the director act on monthly, and what is noise?

tasks.short: Read new law, rulings and CAO texts and say what they mean for us.

today.trigger: A CAO round, the twice-yearly statutory minimum wage change, a forwarded ruling, or the yearly policy review.
steps: Read the CAO texts, government publications and rulings that someone has saved.
Mark what differs from current practice in pay, contracts, working time or absence.
Discuss the impact with compensation, payroll and, when it is material, outside counsel.
Tell management and prepare a works-council item where advice or consent is required.
File the note on SharePoint.
systems: Published statutes, CAO texts and court decisions
drudgery: Reading long PDFs to find the few articles that change a wage component or a contract clause.
Keeping a personal folder of links that the rest of HR cannot navigate.
Writing the same summary three times, for payroll, the works council and the management team.
today.time_sinks: Reading and extracting, in bursts when a CAO is renewed or a statutory rate changes, and again whenever a colleague forwards a ruling.

lenses.faster: A change note arrives with the source passage, the effective date and the likely AFAS or policy consequence, so the first full read of the PDF drops out. The director reads the cited lines and decides.
lenses.autonomous: A watchlist on the two CAOs, the statutory minimum wage dates, and absence and working-time legislation opens a change note when a new text is published, without waiting for someone to forward it.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the reading cost, every material change would be mapped within a week to a wage component, a contract template, a Studytube rule and a works-council agenda item.
lenses.joy: Skimming comparison tables inside a CAO PDF is the part nobody will miss. The judgement on what Noordhaven should concede, and what it should change in the warehouse CAO, stays.
lenses.options: The note can set out several responses, such as apply unchanged, seek a phased introduction, open a works-council consent request, or ask counsel before payroll changes a scale.
lenses.altitude: The director maintains the watchlist, the definition of 'material', and a sample check of citations. Reading every new PDF end to end sits with the monitored set of official texts.
reach: The first reading of a new CAO article against current scales, which the Compensation and Benefits Specialist now does under time pressure.
A dated change list of wage components and allowances for the Payroll Specialist.
The employer-cost effect, premiums and allowances, that the Finance Director needs in the forecast.

tasks.human_edge: What the company will do with a CAO change or a ruling, and what it will say to the works council and the unions, is a position only the director can take. A summary can prepare that position. It cannot hold it.
tasks.pattern_why: The input is unstructured text and the useful output is a structured change note with a citation, a date, who is in scope and which company artefact moves. That note is checkable against the source. It is relied on only after a person confirms the citation.

in_practice.trigger: A new publication on a watched source, a CAO negotiation text saved to SharePoint, or the known January and July statutory minimum-wage dates.
steps: Retrieve the new text from the watched official sources and from the SharePoint copy of both CAOs.
Extract a row per change: citation, effective date, who is covered (drivers, warehouse, office, flex), and which artefact is affected.
Attach the source passage. Produce no article number that is not in the retrieved text.
The director, with compensation or payroll, confirms or discards each row that would change pay, a contract template or a policy.
Confirmed rows become work on the HR operating calendar and, where needed, a works-council item.
in_practice.human_gate: Any row that would change an AFAS wage component, a contract template, a policy or a works-council proposal is confirmed by the director against the cited passage before it is used. Counsel still reviews dismissals, reorganisations and disputes.
data_needed: Current text of CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer and the company's warehouse CAO, with version dates
Published statutes and the rulings the director has put on the watchlist
Current AFAS wage components, scales and contract templates
List of which topics require works-council advice or consent
Name of the outside counsel route for items the note must not decide
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint register of legal and CAO changes, one row per source, with citation, decision and owner.

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot can summarise a CAO or policy PDF the company has stored in SharePoint and can show the passage it used.
Dutch statutes, official CAO publications and court decisions are published as primary texts a watchlist can point at. Reliable article-level extraction still needs a human check against the passage.
A continuous legal monitor that correctly maps a new Dutch ruling onto an AFAS wage component, without a person checking the citation, is not established here.

risks: A wrong article number, scope or effective date flows into payroll and is then defended to the works council as fact.
Arbitration and kantonrechter decisions are easy to over-read. A case about a driver on a night shift is not a rule for a Venlo order picker.
Sending full rulings about identifiable employees to an external model can breach AVG.
If counsel must re-read everything, the hours move rather than fall, and the register becomes another folder.
research_questions: On a blind sample of twenty recent CAO articles and one ruling, how often are the article, the date, the scope and the affected AFAS component right before a human edit?
Which sources does the director trust today, and are the two CAO texts on SharePoint the versions payroll actually uses?
How many hours last year went to reading, and how many to a decision that still needed outside counsel?
Which changes in the last CAO round arrived in AFAS late, and what did that cost in corrections?

tasks.short: Oversee how jobs are described, graded and placed in the function house.

today.trigger: A new role, a regrade request, a vacancy whose pay looks wrong, or a periodic review of the function house.
steps: Compare the proposed duties with the CAO reference functions and the company's warehouse function house.
Ask the compensation specialist for a grade and a salary scale.
Check AFAS for people paid off scale or sitting in an outdated function.
Decide the exception or the change in grade.
Involve the works council when the system itself changes, and the manager when one job changes.
drudgery: Hunting the current function description across SharePoint and old mail.
Line-by-line comparison of duties against a reference function.
Finding employees whose AFAS function no longer matches the work they do, especially where sites invented local titles.
today.time_sinks: The comparison and the data cleanup, repeated each time a role is added or a site uses its own job title.

lenses.faster: A comparison pack already lines the new duties up against the closest reference functions and lists who in AFAS sits near that title. The line-by-line hunt drops out.
lenses.autonomous: A Recruitee vacancy with no AFAS function code and scale, or an employee whose function text and scale disagree, opens an exception for compensation before the vacancy is published.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the comparison cost, every role on three sites would sit on a maintained function house, and local titles such as teamcoach and shift lead would map to one grade and one pay band.
lenses.joy: Searching for the master description and retyping duty comparisons are the parts nobody will miss. The conversation about what a shift leader in Venlo is actually accountable for stays.
lenses.options: The pack can show the two or three closest reference functions, the grade each would imply, and the pay and pension-base difference, for the director and compensation to choose from.
lenses.altitude: The director looks after the function house as a system: who may add a title, when a drift report runs, and when a change is big enough for the works council. Scoring one job sits with compensation, on a pack the director can audit.
reach: The line-by-line comparison the Compensation and Benefits Specialist now does from scratch, with the director keeping the disputed grade.
A block in Recruitee so the Recruiters cannot open a vacancy without a function code and a scale.
A drift list the HR Administrators can clean up: AFAS function against the title managers actually use.

tasks.human_edge: A grade that an employee, a manager or a union will challenge has to be owned by the director and the compensation specialist. Fairness across sites, and the works-council route when the system changes, are not a text-matching exercise.
tasks.pattern_why: The director oversees classification. The comparison of duties with a reference function can be prepared and checked. The grade becomes real only when compensation and the director sign it, because it sets pay for people under two CAOs.

in_practice.trigger: A new or changed role request, a Recruitee vacancy missing a function code, or the twice-yearly drift report.
steps: Match the proposed duties to the closest reference functions in the transport CAO book and the warehouse function house.
Show the differences in duties, the grade each match would give, and the pay range already in AFAS for that scale.
List employees in the same local title whose scale or function code differs, by site.
Compensation recommends a grade. The director accepts it or sends it back.
A change to the function house itself goes to the works council before it is used. A single job change goes to the manager with the approved description.
in_practice.human_gate: No grade, scale or function-house change is entered in AFAS until the director and the compensation specialist have signed it. A system change waits for the works-council route.
data_needed: The current reference-function book for CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer
The company's warehouse function house and its owner
AFAS function, scale, step and site
Recruitee vacancy texts and whether a function code is filled in
Open regrade requests and their outcome
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint function-house register: request, comparison, decision, AFAS function code and date.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit stores function and salary scale on the employee and can list people by function and site.
Recruitee holds the vacancy text and the pipeline, so a missing function code can be seen before publication if the field is used.
Changing a job-evaluation or remuneration system is a works-council consent matter, and a grade that departs from the CAO reference book creates pay and pension-base errors.

risks: A fluent comparison that ignores the CAO reference book will put people in the wrong scale. Payroll and pension contributions then follow the error.
The transport function book may not cover warehouse roles. Forcing a warehouse job onto a driver reference function produces a grade nobody can defend.
Local titles that hide equal work across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo are an equal-pay problem under the equal-treatment rules.
Employees and managers will learn to write duties toward a higher reference function if the pack is treated as the grader.
research_questions: Which book is actually in force for warehouse jobs, and where is the master file with its version date?
How many grades changed in the last two years, and who challenged them: employee, manager, union or works council?
Do Recruitee vacancies carry an AFAS function code and scale before they go live?
What pay gap shows up today for the same duties under different local titles across the three sites?

tasks.short: Forecast how many people each site needs, by role and by season.

today.trigger: The budget cycle, peak-season planning when flex moves between about 150 and 300, or a large customer win or loss.
steps: Start from AFAS headcount, known leavers and the absence rate.
Ask operations and finance for volume by site.
Ask warehouse managers how many agency workers they expect to order.
Build an Excel forecast by role and site.
Turn the gap into vacancies for the recruiters and a flex assumption for finance.
drudgery: Rebuilding last year's workbook and retyping the assumptions.
Chasing volume numbers that sit in operations mail.
Adding agency hours that are not in the AFAS headcount.
today.time_sinks: One heavy build a year, then a forecast that is already stale by the time the peak starts.

lenses.faster: Once volume, productivity, absence and attrition are explicit inputs, the headcount arithmetic is recalculated without rebuilding the workbook. The director spends the cycle on the assumptions.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly refresh runs after the AFAS extract and the agency-hour load. It flags a site where the gap versus the approved plan exceeds the threshold, without a separate request.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the build cost, Noordhaven would keep a rolling 13-week plan by site and role, so permanent vacancies open before the peak and flex orders match real volume.
lenses.joy: Rebuilding the spreadsheet and chasing last year's tab are the parts nobody will miss. The argument with operations about whether Venlo really needs forty extra pickers in November stays.
lenses.options: The same drivers can produce a low, base and high volume path, plus a permanent-versus-flex mix, with the cost at pay parity for agency workers shown on each path.
lenses.altitude: The director owns the planning rules: the drivers, the review rhythm and the rule that a forecast is not yet permission to hire. Running the arithmetic sits with the model FP&A can audit.
reach: Headcount as a driver in the financial forecast the FP&A Analysts maintain.
A month-by-month vacancy opening plan for the two Recruiters, tied to accepted offers already in Recruitee.
A flex-order proposal per site, within the approved plan, for the HR business partners to take to warehouse managers.

tasks.human_edge: The bet on volume, and the choice between a permanent team and a larger flex pool, affects the CAO, the works council and the 90-day north star. Operations and the director have to own that bet. A model can only reprice it.
tasks.pattern_why: With structured inputs and written drivers, next month's heads by site and role are a calculation with a checkable result. A language model is not required for the arithmetic. The director approves the assumptions and the published plan because the plan starts hiring and flex spend.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly, after the AFAS refresh and the agency-hour load, and again when operations issues a revised volume figure or a site gains or loses a large customer.
steps: Load headcount, known leavers, absence rate, certificate constraints, open vacancies and agency hours.
Apply the signed productivity and volume assumptions and calculate the gap by site, role and week.
Price permanent cost and flex cost, including agency pay parity, on the low, base and high paths.
The director reviews the assumptions with operations and FP&A and publishes one path.
Recruiters and HR business partners receive only the approved vacancy and flex numbers.
in_practice.human_gate: The director and FP&A publish the plan. No vacancy is opened and no agency order is treated as approved until that publication. A new customer or a lost contract is an exception the director handles before the next automatic refresh is trusted.
data_needed: AFAS headcount by function, site, contract type and FTE
Known leavers and absence rates, not diagnoses
Agency hours and invoices by site for the three agencies
A volume figure from operations by site and week
Signed productivity assumptions, such as orders per picker hour or stops per driver
Recruitee vacancies and accepted offers with start dates
CAO hours and the pay-parity rules that change the cost of a flex hour
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint workforce-plan folder: input versions, assumption log, published path and the names who signed it.

evidence.claim: Excel and Power BI can run a driver-based headcount model on tables the company already keeps from AFAS.
evidence.source: Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Power BI

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit is the headcount source for permanent and fixed-term staff, while the seasonal swing of about 150 to 300 flex workers is visible only if agency hours are loaded as well.
Dutch agency workers are entitled to pay parity with comparable employees at the hirer, so a flex-heavy plan can cost more than a rough agency rate suggests.

risks: Without a stable weekly volume figure from operations, the model produces a precise number from a guess.
Flex workers missing from AFAS make the baseline too low and the peak gap too high.
Warehouse managers who order flex directly in the three agency portals will ignore a plan that arrives after they have already ordered.
A published forecast gets treated as permission to hire, or as a target that discourages a needed hire.
research_questions: Can operations supply a weekly volume number by site in a stable format, and how often was last year's figure revised after the peak started?
What share of agency hours is in AFAS today, against the three agency portals?
Who currently places flex orders, and would they follow an approved 13-week number?
How far off was last year's headcount forecast by site at the peak, and which single assumption caused most of the miss?

role.altitude: The HR director becomes the person who sets and audits the rules for hire-to-productive: what 'productive and still here at day 90' means, which exceptions reach a human, and whether the rules are fair across Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo and the flex pool. Status assembly, CAO reading and workbook rebuilds sit with checked systems.
reach: The monthly people-cost phasing the FP&A Analysts now build from a separate headcount file.
The CAO-to-payroll change list the Compensation and Benefits Specialist and the Payroll Specialist assemble when a text is new.
The certificate and 90-day retention watch that L&D and the recruiters each keep in their own sheets.
A works-council information pack built from the same figures and the same change register.
The agency-versus-permanent comparison the Finance Director asks for at budget time.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks are about 1,364 hours a year, around 85 percent of this one FTE at a loaded cost of EUR 110 an hour. A large share of the directing tasks is presence: works-council meetings, conversations about a person, site time, and decisions with legal consequence. Those hours compress little. AVG, works-council consent and the EU AI Act employment category cap automated decisions about workers. One director cannot know 1,200 people; the ceiling is attention and trust, and the system only helps if the right exceptions arrive and the director is still believed when they act.
skills_to_grow: Reading a workforce forecast as drivers, volume, productivity, verzuim, attrition and flex share, well enough to challenge each one with FP&A and operations.
Writing the exception rules: the threshold, the owner, and the matters that stay a human decision, including medical data, sanctions and dismissal.
Checking a CAO or legal note against the source passage, including article, date and who is in scope.
Agreeing with the privacy officer and the works council the cell size, purpose and retention of people dashboards.
Judging every proposed HR change against the north star: a hire who is productive and still here after 90 days.
role.ambitious_version: Noordhaven runs a rolling 13-week people plan per site that ties volume, absence, certificates and the vacancy pipeline together, and prices permanent staff against flex at pay parity. The director spends the freed time on the patterns that move the north star: managers whose new hires fail inside 90 days, shifts where verzuim and turnover cluster, and the works-council and CAO choices that decide whether flex stays a seasonal buffer. Policy answers, grades and forecast scenarios arrive as checked drafts with a named owner. The director's signature is the control.
